plugins.description: Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Replaces bb's thread list with one Activity list of every parent thread from every project, latest first, with pinned threads above it and the Working, Asleep and Archived shelves folded at its foot. A filter narrows it to one project, and rows are one line or two. Each row shows the thread's agent, its project's coloured initial, its title, its pull request, how many threads run under it, and its state or how long ago it last moved. Right-click a row for its menu (rename, pin, copy, sleep or wake, archive, delete); under the pointer, its corner offers Archive. A thread put to sleep waits on Asleep until its time, then comes back to the top. Rest on a row for its card: its state and since when, machine, project, branch, pull request, its plan while it works, and a tree of its subthreads to open.

Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Run bb threads on on-demand boat.dev sandboxes that stop when idle, resume on the same disk, and start from the boat saved snapshot, environment and size you pick in the composer, with bb's GitHub login or else boat's.
Wakes your Grok Bots by webhook when a bb thread needs attention: an open question or approval, a finished turn, or a failure.

Cards under the new-thread composer. The first, Activity, is six months of your merged GitHub PRs as a calendar grid, with the threads you started, PRs merged and lines changed; its data refreshes in the background, so it opens instantly. With PR Reviews installed, its pull requests card sits beside Activity.
Agents draw mdxcn figures in chat: callouts, steps, terminals, tables, KPIs, charts, timelines and more, from a fenced block.

A PR Reviews app on the left rail that lists your pull requests across every GitHub project, in Authored by me, Needs my review and Recently merged, with stacked pull requests as trees, and opens each one on a page with its whole diff in a file tree and a guided review, written by a review thread, that walks you through the change step by step. Its Summary shows the PR's activity, as GitHub's Conversation tab does, and every diff shows the PR's GitHub review threads where they belong. It posts to GitHub only the review comments, replies and conversation comments you write or pick from the guide, on your click, and changes a pull request's state only from the state pill on its page; review threads never post to GitHub. A card on the new-thread screen shows the PRs waiting on your review, or your own.
Agents answer data with an inline chart, without being asked, using bb's inline visualizations.

A live strip above the composer that counts the latest prompt's subagents and child threads, plus any still running, and how long they have taken, and opens into one row per subagent that expands to its report and latest steps and opens its full transcript in the side panel or its own thread; a Subagents tab in the side panel lists every subagent in the thread, grouped by the prompt it was launched after.
